{"data":{"repository":{"p0":{"totalCount":1,"nodes":[{"number":3,"url":"https://github.com/yasyf/cc-context/pull/3","title":"docs(ship): correct the --help description of the graphite probe gate","body":"`ccx vcs ship --help` still described the pre-0.39.0 graphite gate:

> a probe that times out or cannot reach the Graphite server keeps the lane
> rather than demoting, so a network blip never pushes a branch outside a real
> stack, and the verdict is cached between ships.

v0.39.0 inverted exactly that. An unanswerable probe now **demotes** — keeping a
lane nobody could confirm is what made the gate inert for four releases, since
every probe was timing out against a 5s cap and every timeout read as "keep".
The help text was the last place the old contract survived, so the binary was
documenting the bug as though it were the design.

It also claimed a flat "cached between ships", which was true when there were two
verdicts and is now three, each on its own span.

## The change

Two places, both saying what the code does: an unconfirmable lane declines, the
trade that makes that the safer half is named, and the three TTLs are spelled out
(a yes for a day, a no for an hour, an unanswered probe for a minute — so an
outage costs one probe a minute rather than one per command).

- `internal/cli/ship.go` — the long `--help` text.
- `plugin/skills/ccx/SKILL.md` — the shipped skill doc, which carried the same
  claim in shorter form. Hand-maintained, not a cc-guides artifact, so it needs
  fixing at the source rather than by re-rendering.

No behaviour change; this is documentation catching up to `baffb08`.

## Also

The same stale claim lived in `plugin/guides/md/ccx.md` over in cc-skills, which
renders into this repo's `AGENTS.md`. That landed separately as
`yasyf/cc-skills@f500d7d`, so the Guides bot will re-render `AGENTS.md` here on
its own.

## Verification

`go build ./...` clean. `ccx vcs ship --help` reads the corrected sentence. There
is no test to add — the string is the artifact.

## Added
- AST chunking for **TSX, CSS, SCSS, Vue** — grammar pins match tree-sitter-language-pack 1.6.2 (semble's chunking dependency); embed grows ~330 KB to ~4.4 MB. Full 63-repo/1251-query NDCG gate re-ran **PASS, benchmark-neutral** (overall delta vs semble unchanged at −0.0007).

## Changed
- **`ccx web search` embeds with the native in-process engine** on the same pinned `potion-base-8M`; the per-call `uv`/Python subprocess is deleted (`embed_driver.py`, `UVEmbedder`, CI HF-snapshot steps). Cached page vectors stay valid (pin string unchanged); offline/no-weights degrades to BM25-only; new golden-vector parity test (WASM vs Python `model2vec`, cosine ≤ 3e-8, observed).
- Embed engine parameterized by `ModelPin` (`CodePin` byte-identical to the old consts — `TestEncodeParity` + fused-search goldens unchanged); weights cache namespaced per model (one-time ~30 MB re-download of the code model).

## Fixed
- Gitignore-negated files with unmapped extensions line-chunk instead of vanishing.
- Index-cache crash safety via a per-write generation nonce across manifest/chunks/vectors (schema bump; torn caches rebuild).
- Malformed UTF-8 now decodes with Python `errors="replace"` parity end to end — including the production indexing path (review finding).
- Weight downloads bounded at 5 min so a stalled mirror can't wedge engine construction (review finding; restores the deleted uv path's first-run bound).
- Embed `Encode` honors context cancellation when queued.

## Verification
- `task test` (`-race`) green ×35 packages; `task lint` 0 issues.
- NDCG gate: PASS (artifacts on cc-notes log `5e69ae9d`).
- Review: gpt-5.6-sol finder + adversarial refuter over the full diff; both confirmed findings fixed with regression tests (`TestIndexDecodesMaximalSubsequences`, `TestDownloadTimesOut`); refuter sweep of cache-nonce orderings and `CodePin` byte-identity came back clean.","isCrossRepository":false,"baseRefName":"main","headRefOid":"012c601c3687845d877216560588308071884082","mergeable":"UNKNOWN","labels":{"nodes":[]},"state":"MERGED","mergedAt":"2026-07-23T06:40:41Z","timelineItems":{"nodes":[{"actor":{"login":"yasyf"}}]}},{"number":1,"url":"https://github.com/yasyf/cc-context/pull/1","title":"Native semantic search: replace semble/uvx with an in-process engine (v0.30.0)","body":"Replaces the external Python \`semble\` dependency (spawned via \`uvx\`) behind \`ccx code search\` / \`ccx code related\` with a native in-process engine. Bit-exact port of semble 0.5.2's pipeline, gated on semble's own benchmark.

## Result (same-machine, semble's 63-repo / 1251-query harness)
- **NDCG@10 0.8527** vs same-machine semble 0.8534 (−0.0007; symbol tied, architecture +0.0003). The gap is 96% our deterministic batch-invariant embedding vs semble's neighbor-dependent pad-polluted batches — proven by a full chunk-injection partition (our chunks are neutral, −0.000025). Shipping this by owner decision; batch-invariance is the more correct behavior.
- **Query p50 1.384 ms** vs semble 1.778 ms — faster.
- **Cold-index median 400.5 ms** vs semble 417.6 ms — faster.

## What's here
- **chunk**: tree-sitter AST chunking via wazero-loaded per-language grammar WASM (19 languages, ~4 MB gzipped embed; line-window fallback otherwise), byte-exact vs semble goldens.
- **embed**: resident model2vec inference — model2vec-rs compiled to WASM, weights (\`potion-code-16M-v2\` @ pinned HF revision) download once into a local cache; cosine parity ≤3e-8 vs Python.
- **rank**: hand-rolled BM25 + RRF fusion + the full ranking stack, exact-parity against semble-generated goldens.
- **index/engine**: semble-parity walker, persistent binary index cache with partial reindex, resident in-process index cache for warm-query serving, and the native search/related orchestration.
- **seam**: \`internal/semble\` and the proxy MCP session deleted (~594 LOC); native render with \`score=\`/\`cos=\` labels; new per-request \`--content\` filter on both CLI and MCP.

## Verification
- Differential golden parity across chunk / embed / BM25 / fused search.
- Full benchmark gate (\`.context/semsearch/gate-ccx-vs-semble.md\`, \`timing-ccx-full.md\`, \`injection-partition.md\`).
- Five-component finder/refuter review; confirmed findings fixed (determinism trio + revision-aware cache keys + embed hygiene + chunk robustness), each with a regression test. Lower-priority findings filed as backlog tasks.
- \`task test\` (-race) + determinism stress (-count=5) green; \`task lint\` 0 issues.

Forty-odd lanes share that repository through linked worktrees, so one run stopped on a conflict, or one whose process died mid-push, refused every other lane's rebase with `a stack rebase is already in progress` until someone ran `continue` or `abort` for it. A run of `yasyf/rv2-generated-inputs` held the slot for seven hours on 2026-09-25.

**One run record per stack.** The record moves to `.git/ccx-stack-rebase/<bottom branch>/state.json`, with the conflict briefs beside it. A run that `--linearize` joins from several stacks claims every bottom branch it touches. The state sits under the first, and a `root` file under each of the others names it. A rebase is refused only when a recorded run shares a bottom branch with it. The claim is a `rename` of a staged directory onto the stack's own, so two processes racing for the same stack cannot both win, and a crash between claiming and writing cannot leave an empty claim behind.

**What holds a run is reported, never reclaimed.** Each run records the pid driving it, and `continue` refreshes it. The refusal names the stack and which of four holders has it, each with the command that clears it.

- A run stopped on a conflict names the workspace to resolve, then `ccx vcs stack continue --stack <bottom>` or `abort --stack <bottom>`.
- A run stopped on a conflict whose workspace is gone names `abort --stack`.
- A run whose pid is still alive says to wait for it.
- A run whose pid exited names `abort --stack` when no branch moved, and `continue --stack` when the stack is rewritten locally and only the push remains.

Nothing is dropped on a timer.

**`--stack <bottom branch>` on `continue` and `abort`.** Without it they resolve the run as before, from the conflict workspace they run in, then the branch checked out, then the only run. With two runs and no way to pick, the refusal lists the `--stack` values. `abort` of a run whose conflict workspace is gone prunes the worktree registration instead of failing in `git worktree remove`.

**The old single record is refused, not migrated.** A `state.json` directly under `.git/ccx-stack-rebase/` is reported with the branches it holds, whether they are rewritten locally, and the `rm -r` to run once nothing drives it.

Tests. `TestStackRebaseRunsTwoStacksSideBySide` takes two stacks through their conflicts and continues them in either order, and picks a run with `--stack` from the other stack's branch. `TestStackClaimAdmitsOneRunPerRoot` races sixteen claims for one stack and expects one winner. Four `TestStackRebaseRefuses*` tests plant a run with an exited pid, a live pid, an applied run, and a conflict whose workspace is gone, then check the holder line and that the named `abort --stack` clears it; `TestStackRebaseRefusesAFlatStateFile` covers the old record. `go test -race ./internal/cli -run 'TestStack'` passes locally.
